judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three long parallel allocation paragraphs; mechanical and internally consistent, if hard to read.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The granting language is garbled in places ('all the right, title and interest of the Sellers in and to the assets in the Mortgage Loans'), and the delivery obligations shift unpredictably between 'the Depositor' and 'the Seller may deliver', with a one-year title-policy grace built into limb (v).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its final paragraph says the Special Deposit 'will be transferred by EMC', while the Special Deposit definition says it is 'deposited into the Trust by the Depositor'; and the conveyance of 'the Trust Fund' must be squared with the Trust Fund definition, which omits the Bring Down Agreements that Section 2.02(d) requires the Trustee to enforce.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains the ungrammatical 'will deliver to the Sponsor, the Sellers, the Trustee an Initial Certification', and the review standard mixes a duty to 'ascertain' with permission to 'conclusively rely' on execution and genuineness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to loans 'identified in Exhibit B to this Agreement, as supplemented', while the Mortgage Loan Schedule definition contemplates amendment for substitutions rather than supplementation; the interaction with Section 2.02(c)'s cure/repurchase remedy is also left implicit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite 180-day review with a stated notification duty; 'appear defective on its face' is a soft but conventional standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires the Custodian to notify only 'the Sellers', whereas Section 2.02(c) makes both the Sellers and the related Originators potential repurchasers of defective loans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence makes cure/repurchase/substitution 'the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Certificateholders or to the Securities Administrator on their behalf' — a limitation that names two persons but conspicuously omits the Trustee and the Trust, an expressio unius problem on the face of the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.02(d) separately empowers the Trustee to enforce repurchase obligations 'on behalf of the Trust', and Section 2.03 provides a separate repurchase mechanic, so the reach of this sole-remedy sentence against those provisions is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The duty extends to repurchase obligations 'and any other obligations of the related Seller or the related Originator under such agreements, including, without limitation' the Sponsor's Accredited backstop — a general catch-all followed by one specific, raising ejusdem generis and expressio unius questions about the backstop's scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence and against the Trust Fund definition, which conveys 'the rights under the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement' but does not mention the Bring Down Agreements the Trustee is told to enforce.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The notice paragraph turns on 'discovery' of a breach that 'materially and adversely affects the interests of the Certificateholders' and requires 'prompt written notice', all elastic terms; the deposit timing is keyed to the Determination Date, of which there are two.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The section is headed as containing only the Master Servicer's and Securities Administrator's representations, yet it houses the substitution and repurchase machinery that the Replacement Mortgage Loan definition, Section 2.05 and Section 4.02 all cross-refer to as if it contained loan-level representations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence survival clause; on its own terms it is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Section 2.03 representations survive 'delivery of the respective Mortgage Loans and Mortgage Files', which makes sense only for loan-level representations, whereas Section 2.03 contains corporate representations of Wells Fargo; the Mortgage Loans definition also cites a non-existent 'Section 2.03(b)(v)' representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final paragraph reads 'Upon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach', omitting a conjunction, and the good-title representation is given without any stated remedy for its breach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Depositor's good-title representation sits against Section 2.01's conveyance and Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence, which addresses only document defects, leaving unclear what follows from a breach of this representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Opens 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of this Agreement' and turns on whether 'default is not reasonably foreseeable', a forward-looking judgment with no decision-maker specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides the repurchase timing in Sections 2.02 and 2.03, which themselves set fixed Determination Date deposit dates, so the two timing regimes must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Gives the Seller or Originator an option among cure, substitution and repurchase 'at such party's option', with a 90-day outside date attaching only to limb (iii).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires substitution to satisfy 'the conditions in Section 2.03', but Section 2.03's substitution paragraph bars any substitution after the second anniversary of the Closing Date, which would leave later-discovered non-qualified mortgages with only cure or repurchase.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limbs (d) and (e) are open-ended catch-alls ('necessary, suitable or convenient ... or are incidental thereto or connected therewith') sitting against three specific purposes, and the final sentence trails off with the dangling 'and this Section 2.07'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (b) says the Trust issues 'the Certificates sold to the Depositor in exchange for the Mortgage Loans', while Section 2.01 and the Preliminary Statement describe the exchange as being for the whole Trust Fund.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grants 'full power and authority to do any and all things which it may deem necessary or desirable' and then imposes a series of specific monitoring duties, so the interaction of the open grant with the specific duties is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The open grant sits against the objective Accepted Master Servicing Practices standard in the same section and against Section 4.05's identically worded grant, which is expressly made subject to the REMIC Provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three specific prohibitions with defined exceptions; reasonably tight, though 'comply with any directions of the Seller, the Servicers or the Master Servicer' is an unqualified obedience duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excepts substitutions 'pursuant to the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement or Section 2.03 of this Agreement', consistently with Section 2.03's substitution paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on the Master Servicer's own 'judgment' and on what it 'deems appropriate', and permits reliance on an Officer's Certificate without further inquiry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out for Wells Fargo as Servicer aligns with Section 4.03(b)-(c), which route Wells Fargo terminations through the Trustee instead.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enforcement standard — such extent and time as the Master Servicer 'in its good faith business judgment, would require were it the owner of the related Mortgage Loans' — is an elastic hypothetical-owner test, and the last sentence's 'Successor master Servicer' is inconsistently capitalised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final sentence conditions the Trustee's assumption of duties on the Trustee 'not been able to find a successor servicer or a Successor master Servicer', which sits awkwardly with the mandatory termination duties earlier in the same subsection and with Section 8.07.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two long parallel reimbursement regimes, each with an 'including, without limitation' list; the trigger 'not fully and timely reimbursed' has no stated deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reimbursement comes from the Distribution Account, and the Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions deduct 'amounts required to be reimbursed pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.03' without mentioning this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Combines an open grant ('any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable, including but not limited to') with four enumerated powers, a classic general-versus-specific tension, and the REMIC proviso turns on what is 'reasonably within its control'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The grant is made 'subject to the REMIC Provisions and the provisions of Article XI hereof', but Article XI is Termination, which has nothing to do with master servicing powers — the cross-reference does not fit.
